newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh stock traders protest at falling prices.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh stock traders protest at falling prices.

text.p: Bangladesh police confronted hundreds of stock traders marching to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's office on Wednesday in a protest over falling share prices.
The protesters scuffled with police, criticised the finance minister and then handed their demands to officials of the prime minister's secretariat, witnesses said.
They called for the removal of Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria for failing to save the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) from what they called manipulators and dishonest brokers.
"Let us have a free market. We want a healthy business atmosphere," one punter said.
The finance minister called for calm.
"It's not at all a crashing situation. The market became overheated and now it's stabilising through correction," Kibria told a news conference. "I appeal to the investors not to panic."
The protesters were mainly from the kerb market that operates outside the DSE building. They face large losses as share prices have dropped to an unexpected low.
They blamed the decline on dishonest brokers, faulty regulations imposed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Kibria's inability to tackle market manipulators.
The DSE index closed 2.41 percent down at 2,718 on Wednesday.
SEC chairman Haroonur Rashid told the news conference the government was considering a contingency plan to salvage the market "if it at all crashes".

"The market can be viewed as normal until the DSE index remains above 1,500 mark. If the index comes down below that level, we will salvage the market under the contingency plan," he said without elaborating.
"Many of us have invested whatever we had, including funds collected through selling of land, in the stock market to overcome pangs of unemployment," trader Shahadat Hossain said.
"But big cats (brokers and DSE members) have made us helpless rats in their paws," he said.
Unless the market moved up in the next few days, the government should be ready to face stronger protests, he said. "We can't just sit idle and watch ourselves dying," another said.
DSE officials said on Wednesday they expected share prices to drop further as both buyers and sellers were being cautious in the volatile market.
Out of 72 issues traded on Wednesday, all but two fell, brokers said. The all-share DSE index was around 3,700 two weeks ago.
